title: How is a customer's payment applied to a demurrage and detention record?
content:
## Scope

This policy of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category governs how a remittance is applied to a per-container record and when the record is settled by payment.

## Policy clauses

1. A remittance is applied to one record, written with the remittance reference exactly as the customer quotes it and the amount remitted.
2. A payment may be booked only on a record whose status is invoiced.
3. A payment may not exceed the record's balance due; any excess is returned by finance and not booked.
4. A remittance reference is recorded only once per record.
5. When the balance reaches 0.00 through payments, waivers and credits, the record is settled, with the settlement date set to that day.
6. A record with a submitted dispute is settled only after the dispute is decided.

The record's status and its earlier payments are read from the line's records before a payment is booked; the reference check looks at the same record and the same reference together.

## Equivalent restatement

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Record not invoiced | No payment is booked on it |
| Amount equal to or below the balance due | The amount may be booked in full |
| Amount above the balance due | Only the balance due may be booked; the excess is returned by finance |
| The same reference was already recorded on this record | It is not recorded again |
| Balance at 0.00 and no submitted dispute | The record is settled that day |
| Balance at 0.00 but a dispute still submitted | Settlement waits for the dispute decision |

## Worked case (hypothetical figures)

A record shows a balance due of USD 300.00 and the customer offers USD 350.00. The payment booked cannot exceed USD 300.00; the remaining USD 50.00 is returned by finance and is not booked.

## Points of judgement

**Q: The customer quotes the reference "AB-77/2" with a slash. How is it recorded?**
A: Exactly as quoted, character for character.
